openings.claim: Connect load-state tags with anonymously confirmed requested windows: removal updates reveal released capacity; confirmation distinguishes intentions from arrivals. Benefit depends on both records staying current.
openings.discriminator: Combined records reduce searches more than updated tags alone or confirmed windows alone.
openings.probe: Compare all three conditions with equal arrival schedules; record search and total per-load recording time. Stop if recording exceeds one minute or identities are required.
openings.uncertainty: Untested; removal-update reliability, anonymous confirmation effort, influence of planned windows on arrivals, and drying-duration variability remain unknown.

openings.claim: Pair removal of an empty hanger tag with a visible vacant-space marker to represent vacancy explicitly. Benefit depends on visual ambiguity causing searches and markers fitting existing racks.
openings.discriminator: Paired changes outperform tag removal alone and existing practice.
openings.probe: Compare those three conditions; measure search time. Stop if markers obscure occupied laundry or require moving another load; retain existing racks and layout.
openings.uncertainty: No effect established; whether released spaces are hard to distinguish and whether markers fit remain uncertain.

lineage.reason: Preserves the coupled state/confirmation dependency, three-condition comparison and recording/privacy gates.
Preserves explicit vacancy, visual-ambiguity dependency, paired-change comparison and physical stopping gates.

decision: Probe separately using existing tags, calendar, pencils and four racks. Across both: never move another resident's laundry, retain racks/layout, keep all per-load recording within one minute, and record no names or apartment numbers. Judge busy-period success by at least nine of ten arrivals finding usable space within three minutes without moving another load. Synthetic observations suggest stale tags and unfulfilled windows; they establish no field effect or tested mechanism.
